title: The Translation of the Meanings of Summarized Sahih Al-Bukhari: Arabic-English
author: Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail Al-Bukhari (compiled by); translated and summarized by Dr. Muhammad Muhsin Khan
publication_date: Summarized translation first published in 1994 by Darussalam Publishers; original Sahih Al-Bukhari compiled in the 9th century CE
target_audience: Muslims seeking authentic guidance from Hadith literature
Non-Arabic speakers wishing to study Sahih Al-Bukhari
Students of Islamic studies and scholars
General readers interested in Islamic texts and history
core_themes: Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh) based on the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad
Guidance on worship, daily life, morality, spirituality, social conduct, and legal rulings
Transmission and authentication of Prophetic narrations
primary_purpose: To make the authentic Hadiths contained in Sahih Al-Bukhari accessible to a global audience through a summarized, bilingual (Arabic-English) presentation, providing guidance, jurisprudential rulings, and insights into the practice and teachings of Prophet Muhammad.

structure_format.organization: Systematically divided into books (kitabs) and chapters, each focusing on specific aspects of Islamic belief, law, or practice; this edition is abridged to include key Hadiths for concise reference
features: Subject-based classification (e.g., faith, prayers, fasting, business transactions)
Occasional explanatory notes or commentary to aid understanding
Summarized presentation—omitting repetitions and less critical chains of narration

key_concepts_lessons: Following the Sunnah (example) of Prophet Muhammad forms an essential aspect of Islamic faith and practice.
Specific rulings and practical advice exist for daily worship and life—such as prayer, charity, honesty in transactions, and manners.
Authenticity in hadith transmission is determined through rigorous chains of narration and verification.
Morality, intention (niyyah), and communal responsibility are recurrent themes.
Islamic legal and spiritual guidance are derived from both Qur'an and Sunnah (Hadith).
notable_features: Summarized to provide ease of reference while preserving authenticity
Dual language (Arabic-English), facilitating study for non-Arabic readers
Considered among the most authentic and influential collections of Hadith in Sunni Islam
Widely used as a reference in Islamic scholarship, religious rulings, and personal study
cultural_historical_context: Sahih Al-Bukhari, compiled in the 9th century CE, is recognized as the most authentic collection of Prophetic traditions (Hadith) in Sunni Islam. The summarized Arabic-English edition, published in the late 20th century, responded to the increasing need among global Muslim communities and researchers for accessible translations of foundational religious texts.
reception_impact: Regarded as essential reading by Sunni Muslims worldwide
Highly respected by scholars and laypeople for its reliability and comprehensiveness
The summarized translation is popular in educational institutions, mosques, and homes
Contributed greatly to making Islamic teachings accessible to non-Arabic speakers
comparable_titles: Riyad-us-Saliheen (The Gardens of the Righteous) by Imam An-Nawawi
The Forty Hadiths of Imam An-Nawawi
Bulugh al-Maram by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
